title: DFT thermochemistry of fuel molecules
action: Perform geometry optimization and vibrational frequency analysis for n-butanol, ethanol, and all gasoline surrogate molecules listed in Burri et al. (Fuel 83, 2004, Table 1) at B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p). Extract molar enthalpy H at 298.15 K and 600 K, and for n-butanol also compute Cp at 298.15 K. Save the results as component_enthalpy.csv.
description: Intermediate table storing pure-component molar enthalpies at the two temperatures needed for mixture calculations.

title: Cp validation for n-butanol
action: Using the DFT-calculated Cp for n-butanol at 298.15 K from Step 1 and the experimental Cp value obtained from NIST, compute the relative error. Output cp_validation.csv with at least one row at 298.15 K.
description: Validation of the chosen DFT level by comparing computed heat capacity of n-butanol with the NIST reference. The acceptance criterion is ≤4% relative error.

title: Mixture enthalpy change analysis
action: From the component_enthalpy.csv, compute per-molecule ΔH = H(600 K) - H(298.15 K). Determine mole fractions for the G100 gasoline surrogate blend using the weight percentages from Burri et al. (2004) and known molecular weights. Then compute mole-weighted ΔH for the following blends: pure n-butanol; G100; G10E (0.9 G100 + 0.1 ethanol); G20E (0.8 G100 + 0.2 ethanol); G10E blended with 60 mol% n-butanol (i.e., 0.4 G10E + 0.6 n-butanol); G100 blended with 40 mol% n-butanol (0.6 G100 + 0.4 n-butanol). **The Blend column must use exactly the strings: n-butanol, G100, G10E, G20E, G10E_plus_60pct_nbutanol, G100_plus_40pct_nbutanol.**
description: Molar enthalpy change for the studied blends. The checker will recompute the mixture values from the component enthalpy table and verify the relative ratios and compensation trends against paper-derived gold benchmarks.
output_schema: Columns: Blend (must be one of: n-butanol, G100, G10E, G20E, G10E_plus_60pct_nbutanol, G100_plus_40pct_nbutanol), Delta_H_kJ_per_mol (float), Delta_H_percent_vs_n_butanol (float).
